facts.statement: The study sought to help design Duchenne muscular dystrophy clinical trials by measuring how timed physical tests and muscle fat levels change over time.
facts.subject: computational

facts.statement: The researchers built six mathematical models using data from the ImagingNMD study and checked them against data from other clinical trials.
facts.subject: computational

facts.statement: Specific mathematical curves were found to best describe how muscle fat and physical test scores change over time.
facts.subject: computational

facts.statement: The models predicted that physical test scores and muscle fat levels reach half of their maximum change between ages 10.6 and 12.8 years.
facts.subject: computational

facts.statement: Using steroids was associated with a later age for reaching half of the maximum change in standing up, climbing stairs, and soleus muscle fat.
facts.subject: computational

facts.statement: Starting test scores and muscle fat levels could reliably predict future changes for standing up speed and vastus lateralis fat in older patients, but not for other measures.
facts.subject: computational

facts.statement: The authors suggest these models can help choose biomarkers and set entry rules for Duchenne muscular dystrophy trials.
facts.subject: computational
